title: Multi-branch union: a string branch listed before int converts every value to text
rationale: Branch identity is not recorded in the flattened form, so the reconstructor re-derives it by trying each non-null branch in declaration order and taking the first that does not throw. The STRING case never throws for any input, so a string branch anywhere before another branch absorbs everything after it. Union member order has no semantic weight in Avro, so fidelity depends on an arbitrary ordering decision.
catchesBugClass: Union branch-tag erasure resolved by permissive coercion. Would go green on a real fix that adds a discriminator column or selects the branch from the runtime Java type.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch loss when two branches are both string-like. It also cannot catch anything on the array-of-records path, which never reaches reconstructUnionValue at all.

predicted.detail: Both values come back as Strings. No member ordering makes both directions correct - the defect is the absence of a branch discriminator, not the ordering.
